To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
East Asians are sensitive to contextual information and that this cultural tendency is also reflected in their art and aesthetic preferences.
East Asians and Western cultures differ in aesthetic preference, which can be explained by cultural differences in attention.
(a) East Asians are more likely than Westerners to attend to the context of an object and (b) East Asians are therefore more likely to prefer context-inclusive artistic styles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how culture shapes aesthetic preference and how aesthetic preference is related to cultural variations in attention.
how culture shapes the way we see, and how it influences our aesthetic preference.
the cultural variations of aesthetic preferences and provides evidence for the role of culture in shaping human aesthetic experience
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attention to context is an important aspect of the cultural variations in aesthetics.
cultural variation in aesthetic preference can be explained in terms of the relation among attentional style, cultural resources, aesthetic preference, and cultural context.
East Asian art is more context-inclusive, and Western art is more object-focused, and this difference is maintained in contemporary art and photography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
East Asians have a more contextual aesthetic preference than Westerners.
cultural differences in aesthetic preference are the result of cultural variations in attentional styles.
the East Asian preference for context-inclusive styles is a result of the cultural resources of East Asian societies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural variations in attention to context are reflected in the cultural variations in aesthetics.
culture shapes the attentional patterns that people use in everyday life and that this is reflected in their art and aesthetics.
culture can shape the way we look at the world.
